column6: Allosteric regulation is reversible conformational control; it contrasts with competitive, not irreversible, inhibition.
Binding at a site other than the active site is the idea allosteric regulation generalizes.
Glucose homeostasis is built on hormones, glycogen and gluconeogenesis; the Cori cycle is an elaboration, not a basis.
The cycle's mechanism runs on NAD+, FAD, CoA, TPP and lipoate.
Classifying sugars helps; monosaccharide isomers is already the hard prerequisite.
Cofactor chemistry (vitamins, metal ions) does not depend on amino acid classification.
Synthesis builds chains of defined length and saturation, which presumes fatty acid structure.
Acetyl-CoA for lipogenesis comes from pyruvate via citrate export.
Wobble is codon-anticodon pairing; it does not draw on how synthetases charge tRNAs.
Glycolysis includes aldose-ketose isomerizations (phosphoglucose and triose phosphate isomerase).
Ketogenesis is fed by fatty acids mobilized from adipose during fasting.
The integration topic covers glucose and fatty acid pathways; cholesterol synthesis is not part of it.
Integration draws on allosteric control (already soft), not on Hill-coefficient analysis.
Fatty acid oxidation is one of the pathways the topic explicitly integrates.
Lipogenesis is one of the pathways the topic explicitly integrates.
Gluconeogenesis is central to the fasted-state response the topic integrates.
Glycogenesis and glycogenolysis are part of the fed/fasted integration.
Kinetic analysis does not use EC classification or naming.
The overview frames where amino-group removal sits in catabolism; the reaction itself stands alone.
Some PTMs (glycosylation, disulfides) act on folding, so folding context helps.
PTMs are covalent changes that do not require translocation machinery; signal-peptide cleavage is a minor case.
PTMs already draw on translation via translation-initiation-and-elongation (hard); this duplicate adds nothing.
Release-factor detail is not needed to understand covalent protein modification.
Folding pathways describe how a chain reaches its native tertiary structure.
Primary structure is a sequence of amino acids; peptide bonds is already the hard prerequisite.
Targeting depends on signal sequences and transport machinery, not lipid or lipoprotein chemistry.
Post-translational mitochondrial import needs chaperone-held unfolded chains.
TGN sorting is a specialization of targeting; the general topic does not draw on it.
The overview frames transamination as the first step of amino acid catabolism.
Translation reads mature mRNA; it does not draw on splicing mechanism.
Glutamate dehydrogenase releases the ammonia the urea cycle disposes of.
Pumps are membrane proteins moving solutes across the bilayer.
The spindle checkpoint at unattached kinetochores restrains APC/C-Cdc20.
Apoptosis is caspase-driven; it does not draw on lysosomal or autophagy machinery.
Chemiosmotic ATP synthesis does not depend on substrate-level phosphorylation beyond a contrast.
Chemiosmosis needs the inner membrane and intermembrane space layout.
The overview places the Calvin cycle in photosynthesis; light reactions is already hard.
Cadherins and integrins are transmembrane proteins linked to the cytoskeleton.
The tissue concept motivates why cells adhere.
An early-grade growth topic is not drawn on by a cell-level unifying-principles topic.
Cell biology intro draws on cell theory, not on the early-grade needs topic.
Cell signaling at this level does not draw on the early-grade responding topic.
p53 triggers apoptosis when damage is irreparable, a core outcome of checkpoints.
Oocyte meiotic arrest is not used to explain somatic checkpoints or cancer.
An organism's life cycle is a different concept from the cell cycle; only the word is shared.
Phase transitions are explained by cyclin-CDK control, not centrosome structure.
Differentiation draws on gene expression and signaling, not the early-grade egg-to-adult topic.
Human growth stages are not used in explaining cell fate specification.
Metamorphosis is not drawn on in explaining transcriptional cell fate programs.
Membrane structure draws on eukaryotic cells and chemistry, not on prokaryotes.
